title: How did you handle FP arms and the TPS body together? Would love to hear your approach
author: haithegreat
selftext:
Hi everyone! I’m working on a small co-op survival game in UE 5.8, mostly together with an AI coding agent, and I’ve hit a wall I’d really appreciate some advice on.

First person is the main view, but in co-op your friends see your full body. The first-person side feels great thanks to KINEMATION’s Survival pack, and the body is a MetaHuman running on Epic’s Game Animation Sample. The tricky part is the third-person view: when I play the first-person animations on the body, the arms pop between states (holding → aiming → throwing), the second hand drifts off the item, and some poses look a bit strange from outside.

**I’d love to know how you approached this:**

Do you use the same animations for FP and TPS, or separate sets?

Has anyone layered a first-person anim blueprint over a motion-matched body? Any tips on the setup?

How do you keep both hands nicely on a held item when switching states?

Did any tool work well for third-person melee or throwing animations?



**Any links, examples or lessons learned would mean a lot. Thanks so much for reading!**

comments.author: Another_3
comments.body:
This is a game dev question, not an AI game dev question. 

Usually you have 2 sets of animations. You can retarget fps to tps
